full_judgment:
5. Defendant no.23 contested the suit by filing written statement contending inter alia that the suit land originally belonged to three brothers Alimuddin Patwari, Monirudin Patwari and Loni Mia alias Loni Patwari in equal share i.e. 1792/3 decimals of land each; C.S. record prepared accordingly; Loni Patwari mortgaged his entire share 1792/3 decimals of land to Jamiruddin Pal,  father of defendant no.23, but failed to pay the loan money in time; Consequently, Jamiruddin Pal filed Money Suit no. 157 of 1921 and after obtaining decree in the suit filed Execution Case No. 506 of 1922; Entire share of Loni Patwari was auction purchased by Jamiruddin Pal; Auction was confirmed on 27.01.1923; Jamiruddin Pal came to know that said property was mortgaged to Tarini Charan Chakrabarti who filed Mortgage Suit No. 16] of 1929 in the Court of Munsif, Chandpur, wherein Jamiruddin Pal was impleaded as a party; Said suit was decreed and Execution Case was also filed; Jamiruddin Pal deposited the decreetal amount and got the property; Jamiruddin Pal mortgaged 98 decimals of land in favour of Basiruddin for a period of 10 years and after 7 (Seven) years redeemed the property; A. Sobhan expired before his father Moniruddin and as such heirs of A. Sobhan did not inherit their grandfather; After expiry of Moniruddin, his two wives Parijan and Rupjan, son Md. Majid, daughters Sabani. Afijan Bibi, Rabeya, Ambia and Ratani Bibi inherited him; A. Majid inherited in total 1.013/48 acres of land and transferred the same to Jamiruddin Pal vide kabala dated 18.12.1942; Jamiruddin Pal through auction and purchase acquired total 2741/6 decimals of land; Jamiruddin Pal died leaving two sons Sadek Ali Pal and defendant no.23 Golam Ali Pal, two daughters Jolekha and Abedennessa; Defendant no. 23 inherited .917/18 decimals of land; Jolekha and Abedennessa transferred their share in favour of their brothers; In this way, defendant no. 23 got .4525/36 decimals of land from his sisters and inherited .917/18 decimals of land and in total acquired 1371/12 decimals of land; S.A. Khatian prepared in his name with other co-sharers; Defendant No.23 alongwith his mother, brother and sisters as plaintiffs instituted Partition Suit No. 83 of 1952 which was decreed on compromise; Present plaintiff no.1 and defendant no. 4 as plaintiffs filed Title Suit No. 393 of 1982, renumbered as Title Suit No. 232 of 1984, for setting aside the said compromise decree; Said suit was decreed on 28.03.1987; Present plaintiff no. 1 and defendant no.4 filed Partition Suit No. 269 of 1981 but subsequently withdrawn the suit with permission to sue afresh; Defendant No. 23 has been possessing and enjoying the suit land on payment of rents and taxes; Plaintiffs are not entitled to get relief in respect of 691271/2880 decimals of land and the suit is liable to dismissed. 

 7. Defendant no. 38 prayed Saham for .33 decimals of land stating inter alia that Moniruddin, Alimuddin and Loni Miah were original owners of the suit land in equal share and accordingly C.S. Khatian prepared in their name; Alimuddin died leaving three sons Younus Patwari, Ismail Patwari and Ishaque Patwari; Said Younus Patwari transferred .18 decimals of land to the defendant no. 38 Most. Khairunnessa vide registered deed dated 29.03.1975; Younus Patwari also transferred .15 decimals of land to defendant No. 38 vide registered deed dated 29.04.1975; Thus defendant no. 38 acquired .33 decimals of land by purchase; Defendant No. 11 Younus admitted said transfer in his application for saham; Defendant No. 38 is entitled to get saham for .33 decimals of land.

 16. Mr. Md. Nurul Amin, learned advocate appearing for the defendant-opposite party nos. 4-6/8/17/21 submits that these opposite parties admit plaint case that share of Loni Patwari was not sold in auction and after the death of Loni Patwari his heirs inherited him to the extent of his 1/3rd share. He also 3 submits that the court below committed an error of law resulting in an error in the decision occasioning failure of justice in not holding that defendant DOS. 23/28-30/32- 36/43(Ka)-43(Umo) though claimed that the share of Loni Patwari was sold in auction but failed to prove their contention by producing credible evidence as such impugned judgment and decree is liable to be set aside. He again submits that defendant no.26, heir of Sadek Ali, who deposed as DW.4 categorically admitted in his cross examination that no auction was held in respect of Loni Mia's share but both the courts below committed an error of law resulting in an error in the decision occasioning failure of justice in not appreciating his testimony in its true perspective. He next submits that the court below committed an illegality in not considering exhibit 'Neo' and 'Neo(1)' i.e. judgment and decree passed in Title Suit No.232 of 1984 by which compromise decree of Partition Suit No.83 of 1952 was set aside on the ground that decree passed in Money Suit No.157 of 1921 and proceedings of Execution Case No.529 of 1922 were exparte as such impugned judgment and decree is liable to be set aside. He thither submits that the defendants who claims auction purchase of Loni Mia's share failed to prove their contention by producing the writ of delivery in support of taking possession through court and the court below committed illegality in passing the impugned judgment and decree without considering these factual and legal aspects as such impugned judgment and decree is liable to be set aside. In elaborating his submissions, learned advocate argued that if Loni Miah's share was sold in auction then S.A. Khatian no. 46 would not be prepared in the name of Alimuddin's heirs and others but the court below failed to consider this legal aspect as such impugned judgment and decree is liable to be set aside. He again submits that certified copy of the sale certificate i.e. exhibit-'Ka' clearly shows that though the sale certificate described boundary of the land but there is no C. S. khatian or plot number and no evidence was produced to prove auction purchase and delivery of possession in favour of the auction purchaser from the land of C. S. khatian no.53 as such impugned judgment and decree is liable to be set aside.
